# Implementation Plan: Phase I - In-Memory CLI Todo Application

**Branch**: `001-phase-1-cli-todo` | **Date**: 2025-12-27 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-phase-1-cli-todo/spec.md`

**Note**: This plan is generated by the `/sp.plan` command following Spec-Kit Plus methodology.

## Summary

Build a Python-based CLI todo application with full CRUD functionality (Create, Read, Update, Delete, Complete/Incomplete) for task management. Tasks are stored in-memory only with no persistence. The application follows domain-driven design principles with clear separation between Task entity, TaskManager service, and CLI presentation layer. Implementation will use Python 3.13+ with UV package manager, adhering strictly to constitutional constraints for Phase I.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Python 3.13+
**Primary Dependencies**: Python standard library only (no external dependencies per constitution)
**Storage**: In-memory only (list/dict structures in Python)
**Testing**: pytest (standard Python testing framework)
**Target Platform**: Cross-platform CLI (Windows, macOS, Linux via terminal/console)
**Project Type**: Single project (CLI application)
**Performance Goals**:
- Application startup < 5 seconds
- Task list viewing < 1 second (up to 100 tasks)
- All operations return to menu < 2 seconds
**Constraints**:
- No file persistence (in-memory only)
- No databases or external APIs
- No external dependencies beyond Python standard library
- Python 3.13+ required
- UV package manager for dependency management
**Scale/Scope**:
- Single-user application
- Support for 100+ tasks without performance degradation
- Menu-driven CLI with 6 operations (Add, View, Update, Delete, Complete, Exit)

## Project Structure

### Documentation (this feature)

```text
specs/001-phase-1-cli-todo/
├── plan.md              # This file (/sp.plan command output)
├── spec.md              # Feature specification (already created)
├── research.md          # Phase 0 output (will be generated below)
├── data-model.md        # Phase 1 output (will be generated below)
├── quickstart.md        # Phase 1 output (will be generated below)
├── contracts/           # Phase 1 output (will be generated below)
│   └── cli-interface.md # CLI menu and interaction contracts
└── checklists/
    └── requirements.md  # Specification quality checklist (already created)
```

### Source Code (repository root)

```text
src/
├── todo_app/
│   ├── __init__.py          # Package initialization
│   ├── models/
│   │   ├── __init__.py
│   │   └── task.py          # Task entity (domain model)
│   ├── services/
│   │   ├── __init__.py
│   │   └── task_manager.py  # TaskManager (business logic)
│   └── cli/
│       ├── __init__.py
│       └── main.py          # CLI interface (presentation layer)
└── __main__.py              # Entry point for `python -m todo_app`

tests/
├── __init__.py
├── unit/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── test_task.py         # Task model unit tests
│   └── test_task_manager.py # TaskManager unit tests
└── integration/
    ├── __init__.py
    └── test_cli.py          # CLI integration tests

pyproject.toml               # UV project configuration
README.md                    # Setup and execution instructions
.python-version              # Python version specification (3.13)
```

**Structure Decision**: Selected **Option 1: Single project** structure because this is a standalone CLI application with no frontend/backend separation or mobile components. The domain-driven architecture is reflected in the three-layer structure:
- `models/` - Domain entities (Task)
- `services/` - Business logic (TaskManager)
- `cli/` - Presentation/interface layer (menu-driven CLI)

This structure supports the constitutional requirement for future extension by keeping layers cleanly separated.
